cards.prompt: You're setting up a new public profile. Fine to share, or keep private?
cards.explanation: Hobbies and things you make are fine. Your school and where you are right now help strangers find you, and your first pet's name is a common security question answer.

cards.prompt: A comment thread says: "Reply with the street you grew up on and your first pet's name to get your elf name!" Your uncle has already replied. What's the risk?

options.text: Those are common answers to account security questions
Only a small one: just people he knows will see his reply
None, because a pet's name and a street can't unlock anything

cards.explanation: Pet names and streets are common security questions, so sharing them can help someone reset his accounts. Comments can also be seen, copied and screenshotted by people he doesn't know.

cards.prompt: Does each app need that permission for its job?
cards.explanation: Allow what fits the app's job: a camera app needs the camera, and a route map needs your location. An alarm clock or a calculator doesn't need your contacts or the microphone.

cards.prompt: Someone you only know from a game chat says they want to send you a gift.

steps.text: They ask: **"What suburb do you live in? And send a photo so I know it's you."** What do you do?

choices.text: Don't send anything, block and report them, and tell a trusted adult
choices.consequence: Right. You're not in trouble, and telling someone keeps you safe.

choices.text: Send them. A gift is a kind thing to offer
choices.consequence: Being friendly online doesn't show who someone really is. Your suburb and a photo help a stranger find you.

cards.explanation: Keep where you live and photos of you away from people you only know online. Block, report and tell a trusted adult.

cards.prompt: What's the safest way to check your bank account at a café?

options.text: Use mobile data instead of the café's Wi-Fi
Pick any network with the café's name in it
Join the Wi-Fi network with the strongest signal

cards.explanation: Anyone can name a fake hotspot after the café, and a strong signal doesn't show who runs a network. Mobile data avoids that risk.

cards.prompt: Match each problem to the privacy setting that fixes it.

pairs.left: Strangers can see all your posts
People you don't know keep messaging you
An app shows people where you are
Photos of you appear on your profile without asking

cards.explanation: A private account hides posts from strangers, friends-only messages stop strangers messaging you, location off hides where you are, and tag review lets you approve photos first.
